questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an english speaking country with similar cultural values as to Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. There was a lot of information, maybe a little to much (i gor a bit overwelmed by the amount).

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a meeting with our study abroad adviser at USYD.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There was a few options. They got filled up pretty quickly. There were both study acommodation similar to what we have in Denmark, but they also had colleges.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I stayed at a college with a full mealplan.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is just as expensive, if not more than in Denmark, but you get to live closer to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There were not certain time lots given for course (on their course website) so it was a bit confusing when I had to choose them. There are  alot of time lots for the course so there is a possibility of overlapping classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Whenever I had any questions I could write to my study abroad adviser.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Chose the classes that you find interesting, both relevant to your degree or not.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They didn't have as many chemistry courses as at UCPH (especially because it was sem 2).

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The course were at a similar level as in Denmark or easier.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UCPH I have fewer lectures, more laboratory and more theoratical exercises than I had at USYD.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Computational chemistry.
Proteins in cells.
Chemistry of biology chemistry.
Molecular self assembly.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend all my course (maybe not Proteins in cells - it was pretty boring and the lecturer was pretty bad at explaining).
The computational chemistry course was the biggest surprise to me - I expected it to be the hardest (as an organic chemist), but it turned out to be my favorite course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Allthough you have health insurance - you will still have to pay to see a doctor (it is cheap though and you may get reimbursed by your insurance.)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
The expenses in Australia is pretty similar to the expenses in Denmark. The public transportation is way CHEAP compared to in Denmark.

Mealplan was included with my accomodation.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: USYD have several gyms, cultural clubs and sport clubs. You could sign up for the chocolate club or play quidditch.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the beach, swim/surf and go for a pint.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go explore as much of Australia as you can. It is a very big country with lovely diverse nature. Go to the beach, for a pint or to a concert.
I spent Christmas and New years in Australia - it was very different, but lovely.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The australian culture is very similar to danish culture. Australians are very freindly, warm and welcoming. We have similar humor and drinking culture, so it is easy to get along with and make australian friends. They find danes exotic.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go for a beer, to the student bar or for a consert.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find big cultural differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are openminded, warm and friendly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy your stay - it is going to be over in no time.
It will be challenging live so far from Denmark, but it is easier than you might think.
It is a bit nerve wrecking meeting new people so far from home, but you will make friends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk to the local students - they will have great recomendations on what to see and do. They will no the best place to go for a beer.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and making new friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The time difference of 10 hours was the biggest challenge, when I wanted to talk to friends and family at home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
